51445331.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant N-terminal His6-tagged human STK3 (18 to 311 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli assessed as dissociation constant by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: Isothermal Titration Calorimetry (ITC). All ITC experiments were performed using NanoITC (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE) at 25 °C in a buffer containing 20 mM Tris (pH 7.5), 150 mM NaCl, and 0.5 mM TCEP. Proteins at 12 μM were titrated into the reaction cell containing the inhibitors. For this protocol, the chamber was pre-equilibrated with the test compound, and the kinase domain of STK3 or STK4 was titrated in while continuously measuring the rate of exothermic heat evolution. The heat of binding was integrated, corrected, and fitted to an independent single-binding site model based on the manufacturer’s protocol, from which thermodynamic parameters (ΔH and TΔS), equilibrium association and dissociation constants (Kₐ and K𝒹, respectively), and stoichiometry (n) were calculated.
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Figure 1. Biochemical characterization of STK3/4 inhibitors. (A) Inhibition of STK3 by 6 using the PhosphoSense CSox-based sensor assay (AssayQuant AQT0135), with fluorescence intensity as a readout (excitation and emission at 360 and 485 nm, respectively). (B) The initial reaction velocity in panel A was plotted against the log compound concentration, and IC₅₀ values were calculated using the log[inhibitor] vs response four-parameter variable slope equation in GraphPad Prism 8 software. (C) Fluorescent thermal melt curves for STK3 and STK4 in the presence of 6, 11, and 32 (20 μM) showing protein thermal shift (ΔTₘ) of >8 °C compared with DMSO. (D) Representative ITC binding data for the interactions between 6 and STK3 and STK4. The normalized heat of binding with the single-site binding fits (red line) is shown, and the raw isotherms of titration heat are displayed as insets. (E) Binding affinities and thermodynamic signatures from isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) for compounds 6 and 32.
original_paragraph.Data Analysis in Results Section: We next sought to determine the crystal structure of compound 6 bound to the kinase domain of STK4. As expected, the structure showed that the pyrrolopyrimidine in compound 6 occupied the ATP-binding site and induced closure of the bilobal kinase domain, restricting the solvent-exposed surface area (Figure 2A). The pyrrole moiety of the pyrrolopyrimidine core formed part of a two-point backbone interaction with the hinge Glu103 and Cys105. The pyrimidine group was also observed to form a hydrogen bond with a bound water molecule. The morpholine group was packed underneath the glycine-rich loop, probably via van der Waals interactions with Gly37 and Val44. The chlorine atom on the phenyl ring of 6 formed an electrostatic contact with the salt bridge between Lys59 and Glu73, indicative of an active kinase conformation. Although the inhibitor was positioned proximally to the DFG loop, no specific polar contacts were formed between compound 6 and Asp167. From a geometric standpoint, there is no obvious steric clash to explain the high affinity of 3-chlorophenyl derivative 6. However, the meta position halogen group is proximal to the hydrophobic back pocket created by Met77 and gatekeeper residue Met102. These residues are widely known to contribute to both affinity and selectivity and have been used in the design of other potent kinase inhibitors. Also likely influencing selectivity, the structures of PF-06447475 bound to LRRK2 surrogates STK24 (PDB entry 4U8Z) and mutagenized CHK1 (PDB entry 5OP5) revealed water-bridged interactions of the CN with the counterparts to the salt pair residues Lys59 and Glu73. On the basis of our co-crystal structure, side chains for Lys59 and Glu73 co-mingle with both the meta chloro of 6 and the amide of 11 and are therefore likely to impart selectivity as a consequence of either bound water displacement or formative polar interactions. For 16, the structural evidence for selectivity for STK3 and STK4 over LRRK2 is less apparent. The hydroxyl moiety does protrude from the binding pocket, and this might serve to stabilize a ligand-induced binding surface.

original_paragraph.Results section - ITC: We also used isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC)²⁹ to determine the thermodynamic properties of the compounds. Analysis of compounds 6 and 32 with STK3 and STK4 demonstrated low nanomolar affinities (ITC-K𝒹) that were comparable to the kinetic measurements (Figure 1D,E). Both compounds exhibited enthalpy-driven thermodynamic profiles in their binding to STK3 and STK4. Apart from strongly favorable binding enthalpy, entropy values are also favorable (Figure 1E).
